title: By nine months, most babies look for an object that dropped out of sight
summary: The CDC says that by nine months, most babies look for objects when dropped out of sight, such as a spoon or a toy.
body: The CDC's nine-month page lists, under cognitive milestones, looking for objects when dropped out of sight, and it gives a spoon or a toy as the example. The line is one item in what the page says most babies do by nine months. A baby who does not do it yet is not classified by the line. The wording belongs to the US CDC list.

sources.title: Milestones by 9 Months
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: US CDC page, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports the cognitive item 'Looks for objects when dropped out of sight (like his spoon or toy).'
